readings.title: The Sin Offering for the Anointed Priest
readings.subtitle: A young bull is offered, and its blood is applied to the incense altar and the altar of ascending offering.
readings.text: [Leviticus 4:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, ‘When a being sins by mistake against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which are not to be done, and shall do any of them:</dq> [3] <dq>‘If the anointed priest sins, bringing guilt on the people, then he shall bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his sin which he has sinned a young bull, a perfect one, as a sin offering,</dq> [4] <dq>and he shall bring <dn>את</dn> the bull to the door of the Tent of Appointment before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and shall lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slay <dn>את</dn> the bull before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And the anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring <dn>את</dn> it to the Tent of Appointment,</dq> [6] <dq>and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in front of the veil of the set-apart place.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And the priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the slaughter-place of sweet incense before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which is in the Tent of Appointment, and pour <dn>את</dn> all the blood of the bull at the base of the slaughter-place of the ascending offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [8] <dq>‘Then he takes <dn>את</dn> all the fat of the bull as the sin offering, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat which is on the entrails,</dq> [9] <dq>and <dn>את</dn> the two kidneys and the fat that is on them by the loins, and the appendage on the liver, which he removes with the kidneys,</dq> [10] <dq>as it was taken from the bull of the slaughtering of peace offerings. And the priest shall burn them on the slaughter-place of the ascending offering.</dq> [11] <dq>‘But <dn>את</dn> the skin of the bull, and <dn>את</dn> all its flesh, with its head and legs, its entrails and dung –</dq> [12] <dq>all of the bull – he shall bring outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. Where the ashes are poured out it is burned.</dq>

readings.title: The Sin Offering for the Congregation
readings.subtitle: When the entire assembly sins by mistake, a young bull is offered in the same manner as for the priest.
readings.text: [Leviticus 4:13] <dq>‘And if the entire congregation of Yisra’ěl strays by mistake, and the matter has been hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which are not to be done, and shall be guilty,</dq> [14] <dq>when the sin which they have sinned becomes known, then the assembly shall bring a young bull for the sin, and bring <dn>את</dn> it before the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the bull shall be slain before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And the anointed priest shall bring some of the bull’s blood to the Tent of Appointment,</dq> [17] <dq>and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in front of the veil,</dq> [18] <dq>and put some of the blood on the horns of the slaughter-place which is before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which is in the Tent of Appointment, and pour all the blood at the base of the slaughter-place of ascending offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [19] <dq>‘Then he takes <dn>את</dn> all the fat from it and shall burn it on the slaughter-place.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And he shall do with the bull as he did with the bull as a sin offering – so shall he do it. And the priest shall make atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And he shall bring <dn>את</dn> the bull outside the camp, and burn <dn>את</dn> it as he burned <dn>את</dn> the first bull. It is a sin offering for the assembly.</dq>

readings.title: The Sin Offering for a Ruler
readings.subtitle: A male goat is offered, and its blood is applied to the horns of the altar of ascending offering.
readings.text: [Leviticus 4:22] <dq>‘When a ruler sins, and by mistake has done against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> which are not to be done, and shall be guilty,</dq> [23] <dq>or if his sin which he has sinned is made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering a buck of the goats, a male, a perfect one.</dq> [24] <dq>‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and slay <dn>את</dn> it at the place where they slay the ascending offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a sin offering.</dq> [25] <dq>‘And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the slaughter-place of ascending offering, and pour its blood at the base of the slaughter-place of ascending offering,</dq> [26] <dq>and burn all its fat on the slaughter-place, like the fat of the slaughtering of the peace offerings. And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq>

readings.title: The Sin Offering for a Common Person
readings.subtitle: A female goat or a female lamb is offered, with its blood applied to the altar of ascending offering.
readings.text: [Leviticus 4:27] <dq>‘And if any being of the people of the land sins by mistake by doing against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which are not to be done, and shall be guilty,</dq> [28] <dq>or if his sin which he has sinned shall be made known to him, then he shall bring as his offering a female goat, a perfect one, for his sin which he has sinned.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slay <dn>את</dn> the sin offering at the place of the ascending offering.</dq> [30] <dq>‘And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the slaughter-place of ascending offering, and pour all the blood at the base of the slaughter-place,</dq> [31] <dq>then remove <dn>את</dn> all its fat, as fat is removed from the slaughtering of the peace offerings. And the priest shall burn it on the slaughter-place for a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And if he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he brings a female, a perfect one.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slay <dn>את</dn> it as a sin offering at the place where they slay the ascending offering.</dq> [34] <dq>‘And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and shall put it on the horns of the slaughter-place of ascending offering, and pour all the blood at the base of the slaughter-place.</dq> [35] <dq>‘Then he removes <dn>את</dn> all its fat, as the fat of the lamb is removed from the slaughtering of the peace offerings. And the priest shall burn it on the slaughter-place, according to the fire offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. So the priest shall make atonement for his sin that he has sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq>

readings.title: Offerings for Specific Trespasses
readings.subtitle: Laws concerning withholding testimony, touching unclean things, or rash oaths, with provisions for the poor.
readings.text: [Leviticus 5:1] <dq>‘And when a being sins in that he has heard the voice of swearing, and is a witness, or has seen, or has known, but does not reveal it, he shall bear his crookedness.</dq> [2] <dq>‘Or when a being touches any unclean matter, or the carcass of an unclean beast, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of unclean creeping creatures, and it has been hidden from him, he is unclean and guilty.</dq> [3] <dq>‘Or when he touches uncleanness of man, any of his uncleanness by which he is unclean, and it has been hidden from him, when he shall know it, then he shall be guilty.</dq> [4] <dq>‘Or when a being swears, speaking rashly with his lips to do evil or to do good, whatever it is that a man swears rashly with an oath, and it has been hidden from him, when he shall know it, then he shall be guilty of one of these.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And it shall be, when he is guilty of one of these, that he shall confess that in which he has sinned,</dq> [6] <dq>and shall bring <dn>את</dn> his guilt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his sin which he has sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a female goat as a sin offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him, for his sin.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And if he is unable to bring a lamb, then he shall bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, he who has sinned, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and the other for an ascending offering.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And he shall bring them to the priest, who shall bring near that which is for the sin offering first, and nib off its head from its neck, but not sever it.</dq> [9] <dq>‘And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the slaughter-place, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the slaughter-place. It is a sin offering.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And he shall prepare the second as an ascending offering according to the right-ruling, and the priest shall make atonement for him, for his sin which he has sinned, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [11] <dq>‘But if he is unable to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he who sinned shall bring for his offering one-tenth of an ěphah of fine flour as a sin offering. He puts no oil on it, nor does he put any frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And he shall bring <dn>את</dn> it to the priest, and the priest shall take his hand filled with it as a remembrance portion, and burn it on the slaughter-place according to the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a sin offering.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And the priest shall make atonement for him, for his sin that he has sinned in any of these, and it shall be forgiven him. And it shall be the priest’s, like a grain offering.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Guilt Offering for Unintentional Sins
readings.subtitle: A ram is offered for sins committed by mistake against the set-apart matters of YeHoVaH, with restitution plus one-fifth.
readings.text: [Leviticus 5:14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [15] <dq>“When a being commits a trespass, and has sinned by mistake against the set-apart matters of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, then he shall bring to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> as his guilt offering <dn>את</dn> a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation in sheqels of silver according to the sheqel of the set-apart place, as a guilt offering.</dq> [16] <dq>“And he shall make good for the sin that he has done against that which is set-apart, and shall add one-fifth to it and give it to the priest. And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and it shall be forgiven him.</dq> [17] <dq>“And when any being sins, and has done what is not to be done, against any of the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, though he knew it not, yet he shall be guilty and shall bear his crookedness.</dq> [18] <dq>“Then he shall bring to the priest a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation, as a guilt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for his mistake he committed unintentionally, though he did not know it, and it shall be forgiven him –</dq> [19] <dq>it is a guilt offering, he was truly guilty before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: The Guilt Offering for Sins Against a Neighbor
readings.subtitle: For sins of deception, robbery, or false swearing, one must make full restitution plus one-fifth and offer a ram.
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“When any being sins, and committed a trespass against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and has lied to his neighbour about a deposit, or about a pledge, or about a robbery, or shall extort from his neighbour,</dq> [3] <dq>or has found what was lost and has lied concerning it, or did swear falsely, so that he sins in regard to any one of all these that a man does,</dq> [4] <dq>then it shall be, when he sins, and shall be guilty, that he shall return <dn>את</dn> what he took by robbery, or <dn>את</dn> what he has extorted, or <dn>את</dn> the deposit which was deposited with him, or <dn>את</dn> the lost item which he found,</dq> [5] <dq>or all that about which he swore falsely. He shall repay <dn>את</dn> its total value, add one-fifth more to it, and give it to whom it belongs, on the day of his guilt offering.</dq> [6] <dq>“Then he brings <dn>את</dn> his guilt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a ram, a perfect one, from the flock, with your valuation, as a guilt offering, to the priest.</dq> [7] <dq>“And the priest shall make atonement for him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he shall be forgiven for whatever he did that made him guilty.”</dq>

readings.title: The Law of the Ascending Offering
readings.subtitle: The fire on the slaughter-place must be kept burning continually, and the priest must handle the ashes properly.
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [9] <dq>"Command Aharon and his sons, saying, ‘This is the Torah of the ascending offering: This is the ascending offering, because it is burned on the slaughter-place all night until morning, and the fire of the slaughter-place is kept burning on it.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and put his linen trousers on his body, and shall take up <dn>את</dn> the ashes of the ascending offering which the fire has consumed on the slaughter-place, and shall put them beside the slaughter-place.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And he shall take off <dn>את</dn> his garments, and put on other garments, and shall bring <dn>את</dn> the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And the fire on the slaughter-place is kept burning on it, it is not put out. And the priest shall burn wood on it every morning, and arrange the ascending offering on it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings –</dq> [13] <dq>fire is continually kept burning on the slaughter-place, it is not put out.</dq>

readings.title: The Law of the Grain Offering
readings.subtitle: A portion is burned as a remembrance, and the remainder is eaten by the priests as a most set-apart food.
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:14] <dq>‘And this is the Torah of the grain offering: The sons of Aharon shall bring it near before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in front of the slaughter-place,</dq> [15] <dq>and shall take from it with his hand from the fine flour of the grain offering, and from its oil, and all the frankincense which is on the grain offering, and shall burn it on the slaughter-place for a sweet fragrance, as its remembrance portion to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [16] <dq>‘Then Aharon and his sons eat the rest of it. It is eaten with unleavened bread, in the set-apart place. They eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [17] <dq>‘It is not baked with leaven. <dn>I</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> it to them as their portion of <dn>My</dn> offerings made by fire, it is most set-apart, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.</dq> [18] <dq>‘All the males among the children of Aharon eat it – a law forever in your generations concerning the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. All that touches them is to be set-apart.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Priest's Anointing Offering
readings.subtitle: A daily grain offering for the anointed priest, which must be completely burned and not eaten.
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [20] <dq>“This is the offering of Aharon and his sons, which they bring near to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, beginning on the day when he is anointed: one-tenth of an ěphah of fine flour as a daily grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.</dq> [21] <dq>“It is made on a griddle with oil. Bring it in mixed, bring the baked portions of the grain offering near, a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [22] <dq>“And the anointed priest from among his sons, who is in his place, prepares <dn>את</dn> it – a law forever to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. All of it has to be burned,</dq> [23] <dq>and every grain offering for the priest is completely burned, it is not eaten.”</dq>

readings.title: The Law of the Sin Offering
readings.subtitle: The priest who offers it eats it, but any sin offering whose blood is brought into the Tent of Appointment must be burned.
readings.text: [Leviticus 6:24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [25] <dq>“Speak to Aharon and to his sons, saying, ‘This is the Torah of the sin offering: In the place where the ascending offering is slain, the sin offering is slain before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, it is most set-apart.</dq> [26] <dq>‘The priest who is making atonement eats <dn>את</dn> it, in the set-apart place it is eaten, in the courtyard of the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [27] <dq>‘All that touches its flesh is to be set-apart. And when its blood is sprinkled on any garment, you wash that on which it was sprinkled, in a set-apart place.</dq> [28] <dq>‘But the earthen vessel in which it is cooked is to be broken. And if it is cooked in a bronze pot, then it is scoured and rinsed in water.</dq> [29] <dq>‘Every male among the priests eats it, it is most set-apart.</dq> [30] <dq>‘And no sin offering from which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Appointment, to make atonement in the set-apart place, is eaten, it is burned with fire.</dq>
